company.description: Amwaste provides non-hazardous solid waste collection, transfer, landfill, and recycling services in the Southeastern United States. company.name: Regional Rail, LLC
company.description: Regional Rail owns and operates short-line freight railroads and related rail services across the United States and Canada. Its customer base spans industrial, agricultural, chemicals, aggregates, food, and logistics end markets that depend on local freight connectivity and transload services. The company follows an asset-heavy operating model built around owned and leased track, rail-served industrial infrastructure, and operating railroad franchises. company.name: Stillhouse Solar Project
company.description: Stillhouse is a utility-scale solar project in Bell County, Texas. Its customer base is the ERCOT market and contracted corporate offtakers, including Hyundai affiliates under a long-term power purchase arrangement. The project follows an asset-heavy contracted generation model centered on long-lived photovoltaic infrastructure. Public disclosures describe a 210 megawatt AC and approximately 281 to 284 megawatt DC solar facility that reached completion in 2025 and commercial operations in 2026. Matrix Renewables acquired the late-stage project from OCI in 2023 and remains the project sponsor. Northleaf Capital Partners became a minority investor through the Stillhouse TEP LLC tax partnership in 2024; Acadia Infrastructure Capital sourced preferred equity and facilitated an environmental-attribute transaction but is not identified as an owner.

company.name: Catalyze
company.subsector: Distributed solar, battery storage, and EV charging infrastructure
company.description: Catalyze develops, finances, owns, and operates distributed solar, battery storage, and EV charging assets in the United States. Its customer base includes commercial and industrial real estate owners, business operators, public-sector counterparties, and community-solar subscribers. The company follows an asset-heavy independent power producer and developer model, with revenues supported by long-term contracts, leases, and other recurring project cash flows. Public materials describe a national platform active across more than 30 states, and recent financings support portfolios including 79 MW of New York community-solar projects and 100 MW of projects in New York, Illinois, California, and Virginia. Catalyze was founded in 2017 and has expanded through project development, operating portfolio growth, and structured financing transactions. EnCap invested in 2019, and Actis acquired a co-control stake alongside EnCap in February 2023 through Actis Energy 5; percentage ownership is not publicly disclosed.

company.name: Alpha Generation, LLC
company.subsector: Thermal generation infrastructure and independent power production
company.description: AlphaGen manages and operates a large portfolio of gas- and oil-fired generation assets in major U.S. power markets. Its customer base is primarily wholesale power, capacity, and ancillary-services markets across PJM, NYISO, ISO-NE, and CAISO rather than retail end users. The platform follows an asset-heavy model built around dispatchable generating facilities and associated development, repowering, and grid-upgrade opportunities. Public disclosures describe approximately 13 to 14 gigawatts of capacity across 23 to 24 facilities in six states and nearly $2 billion of annual revenue at formation. The portfolio is concentrated in strategic markets where reliability, peaking capacity, and time-to-power have gained importance as electricity demand has risen. ArcLight created AlphaGen in January 2024, and ADIA agreed a $500 million minority investment in January 2025; a 2026 New York regulatory ruling identifies ArcLight Fund VII as the controlling sponsor and discloses ADIA's indirect 16.8% interest through Black Volt B 2024 LLC.

company.name: Doral Renewables LLC
company.description: Doral Renewables develops, owns, and operates utility-scale solar and storage projects in the United States. Its customer base consists of utilities, corporate offtakers, and wholesale power markets that contract for power, renewable attributes, and grid services. The business follows an asset-heavy independent power producer model with a large development pipeline and direct ownership of utility-scale projects. Public disclosures describe a development portfolio of more than 13 gigawatts across 18 states, anchored by the multi-phase Mammoth Solar development in Indiana. The company combines project development, financing, construction, and long-term ownership, with a focus on utility-scale and agrivoltaic projects. APG invested $400 million on behalf of ABP in 2024 and was described as the largest individual shareholder following the closing.

company.name: Duquesne Light Company
company.description: Duquesne Light Company is the regulated electric transmission and distribution utility serving more than 600,000 customers across Allegheny and Beaver counties, including Pittsburgh, over an approximately 812-square-mile service territory. The company does not generate power and maintains approximately 8,400 miles of transmission and distribution lines. Its parent, DQE Holdings LLC, discloses three current ownership vehicles: GIC affiliate Epsom Investment Pte. Ltd. at 44.4%, Manulife/John Hancock and PGGM vehicle Three Rivers Utility Holdings, LLC at 30.4%, and APG/CalSTRS vehicle AIA Montana LLC, managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners, at 25.2%. Macquarie's former infrastructure ownership was realized in 2016.

milestones.event: The present Duquesne Light Company was formed on November 15, 1912 through the consolidation of three predecessor utilities.
Duquesne Light Holdings completed its take-private by a Macquarie-led infrastructure consortium in May 2007.
Epsom Investment Pte. Ltd., a GIC affiliate, acquired DUET's interests in DQE Holdings; Duquesne reports GIC as an owner since 2011 and its current stake as 44.4%.
Macquarie Infrastructure and Real Assets sold its 30.4% DQE Holdings interest to PGGM and John Hancock through Three Rivers Utility Holdings, LLC.
AIA Montana LLC, owned by APG Americas Infrastructure and CalSTRS and managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners, became a DQE Holdings owner; its current vehicle interest is 25.2%.

company.name: Gemini Solar + Storage
company.description: Gemini Solar + Storage is an operating 690 MWac solar photovoltaic and 380 MW / approximately 1,416 MWh battery storage project in Clark County, Nevada, developed by Quinbrook with its portfolio company Primergy. The co-located facility supplies NV Energy under a 25-year power purchase agreement and is designed to meet approximately 10% of Nevada's peak power demand. APG acquired a 49% interest on behalf of ABP in 2022. In April 2024, Quinbrook's Valley of Fire Continuation Fund LP acquired the remaining 51%, and the project reached full commercial operations in 2024. A February 2026 refinancing continued to identify the same 51% Quinbrook / 49% APG ownership structure.

milestones.event: Quinbrook acquired the Gemini project and began its development with portfolio company Primergy.
The U.S. Department of the Interior approved Solar Partners XI LLC's plan to construct the 690 MW Gemini Solar Project on federal land northeast of Las Vegas.
APG acquired a 49% equity interest in Gemini on behalf of pension fund client ABP during construction.
Quinbrook's Valley of Fire Continuation Fund LP acquired a 51% interest in Gemini from Quinbrook's Low Carbon Power Fund and other equity holders; APG retained 49%.
Primergy and Quinbrook announced that Gemini had reached full commercial operations in Clark County, Nevada.

company.description: I-66 Express Mobility Partners, LLC is the private concessionaire and operator of the 66 Express Outside the Beltway managed lanes in Northern Virginia, also known as Transform 66 Outside the Beltway. Under a 50-year DBFOM agreement with the Virginia Department of Transportation through 2066, the company financed, delivered, operates, and maintains a 22.5-mile corridor from I-495 to Route 29 in Gainesville. The approximately $3.7 billion project includes two express lanes and three rebuilt general-purpose lanes in each direction, interchange upgrades, more than 4,000 park-and-ride spaces, transit funding, and 18 miles of shared-use path. The full corridor opened ahead of schedule in November 2022. Ferrovial's audited 2025 filing reports Cintra at 55.7%, Meridiam Infrastructure S.a.r.l. at 29.75%, and I-66 Blocker (APG) at 14.55%.

company.name: LBJ Infrastructure Group, LLC
company.description: LBJ Infrastructure Group, LLC is the concession company and TIFIA borrower for LBJ Express, a managed-lanes toll concession in Dallas County, Texas. Under a 52-year DBFOM comprehensive development agreement with the Texas Department of Transportation through 2061, the company financed, reconstructed, operates, and maintains approximately 13.25 miles of I-635 and I-35E, including dynamically priced managed lanes alongside rebuilt general-purpose and frontage roads. The project reached financial close in June 2010, began construction in January 2011, and fully opened in September 2015. Ferrovial's SEC-filed May 2026 factbook reports Cintra at 54.60%, APG at 28.33%, and Meridiam at 17.07%; Meridiam's current portfolio page identifies the corresponding non-Cintra vehicles as LBJ Blocker and MI LBJ.

The concession completed a refinancing that included approximately $615 million of tax-exempt private activity bonds replacing the original 2010 bonds.

company.name: Pattern Energy Group LP
company.subsector: Wind, solar, storage, and transmission development
company.description: Pattern Energy Group LP is a San Francisco-headquartered developer, owner, and operator of utility-scale wind, solar, energy storage, and transmission infrastructure across North America. The company reports 46 operating facilities totaling approximately 12 GW and a 40 GW development and active-construction portfolio. CPP Investments has owned the platform since the March 2020 take-private and holds 69.1% after Pattern completed its share-based acquisition of CPP-owned Cordelio Power on April 2, 2026. On June 9, 2025, an APG- and ART-headed consortium that also included a CalSTRS buyer vehicle acquired Riverstone's entire stake alongside Pattern management; the individual consortium and management stakes were not disclosed. Riverstone had backed Pattern since its 2009 formation and rolled its interest through the 2020 combination before exiting in 2025.

company.name: Brightspeed
company.ownershipVehicle: Apollo-managed funds (including AIOF II Connect Holdings, L.P.)
company.description: Brightspeed owns and operates wireline telecommunications and fiber broadband infrastructure across 20 U.S. states from Charlotte, North Carolina. Apollo-managed funds completed the acquisition of Lumen's incumbent local exchange carrier operations in October 2022. The FCC's 2022 approval order for the subsequently consummated acquisition shows that the Apollo ownership group included AIOF II Connect Holdings, L.P., a vehicle of Apollo Infrastructure Opportunities Fund II, with a direct interest of less than 5% alongside larger Apollo private-equity and co-invest vehicles; the 2% equity and 3% voting values appeared only in the December 2023 proposed post-Mubadala structure. Mubadala signed a $500 million minority investment through CEPSA Holding LLC in May 2023, and the FCC approved the proposed foreign-ownership structure in December 2023; no public legal-closing announcement or date was found, so Mubadala remains a signed pending incoming investor in this census. Brightspeed completed a debt recapitalization in August 2024 that issued warrants and preferred stock, and the current exact ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed. No Apollo or Mubadala exit was found through August 8, 2026.

The FCC approved Brightspeed's proposed post-Mubadala foreign-ownership structure, which showed pro forma interests of 2% equity for AIOF II and approximately 28% proposed equity for Mubadala through CEPSA Holding LLC.

Brightspeed completed a debt recapitalization that secured approximately $3.7 billion of new financing, eliminated approximately $1.1 billion of debt and issued warrants and preferred stock to participating lenders.

company.description: Noble Environmental is a Pittsburgh-headquartered, vertically integrated waste-management platform serving municipalities and commercial customers across the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic and Midwest United States. Founded in 2016, it provides solid-waste collection, hauling, transfer and disposal services through a portfolio of landfills, transfer stations and hauling operations, and it develops renewable-natural-gas facilities that convert landfill gas into pipeline-quality fuel. Apollo-managed funds acquired a majority interest by May 2026; the exact stake, specific fund, legal vehicle and separate legal closing date are not publicly disclosed.

milestones.event: Noble Environmental was founded as a regional waste-management company serving communities and commercial customers from the Pittsburgh area.
